html:
An Indian strategy game played on a board of eight by eight squares, first known around the 7th century CE. Most chess historians think it is the common ancestor of chess and its Asian cousins.

The name is Sanskrit for "four limbs", the four divisions of an ancient Indian army: infantry, cavalry, elephants and chariots. Those became the pieces, along with a king and his counsellor. Pawns moved forward and promoted, the horse moved as the knight still does, and the aim was to trap the king. Many details of the rules are not known for sure. An early reference comes from the court of Harsha in the 7th century.

How it spread:

  • West. It went to Sasanian Persia, where it was called chatrang; a Persian story tells of an Indian king sending the game to Khosrow I as a challenge, and the Shahnameh retells it (chess reaches Persia). The Arabs took it up as shatranj, and it reached Europe through al-Andalus and Italy around the 10th century. In Spain in the late 1400s the counsellor became the powerful queen, and modern chess was born.
  • East. It is thought to have given rise to xiangqi in China, janggi in Korea, shogi in Japan, and makruk in Thailand.
sum: An Indian strategy game played on a board of eight by eight squares, first known around the 7th century CE. Most chess historians think it is the common ancestor of chess and its Asian cousins.
